author_claim: Text of edition is based upon Codex Vaticanus as primary witness; where Vaticanus fails Codex Alexandrinus supplies the text
short_quote: The text of the Vatican MS. has been taken as the foundation of the work... where B fails, A takes its place.
qualification: Vaticanus B chosen as earliest and most valuable single manuscript witness

author_claim: In Genesis where Vaticanus exhibits a lacuna from 1:1 to 46:28 Codex Alexandrinus supplies the running text collated against Cottonianus and Bodleianus
short_quote: The considerable lacunae of B in Genesis... Hence in Genesis i. 1—xlvi. 28 the text is taken from A.
qualification: Codex B lacuna directly affects Genesis 2:24 and Genesis 15:6

author_claim: Apparatus is restricted to the primary extant uncial manuscripts rather than cursive witnesses or daughter versions
short_quote: The notes are confined to the variants of the principal Uncial MSS.
qualification: Manual edition scope does not attempt full genealogical apparatus

author_claim: Orthography strictly reflects the manuscript archetype rather than classical or standardized conventions
short_quote: The orthography of the MS. which supplies the text has been faithfully followed.
qualification: Preserves historical itacisms and scribal forms such as πειν for πιειν in Exod 32:6

author_claim: Accents and breathings are supplied editorially as early uncial hands generally lack them with exception of Codex Ambrosianus
short_quote: Accents and breathings are not found in the earliest MSS., with the remarkable exception of F.
qualification: Codex Ambrosianus F exhibits breathings and accents prima manu

author_claim: Distinct scribal hands and ancient correctors are classified by systematic superscript notations
short_quote: Corrections by the original scribe are marked B* or A*; corrections by ancient hands Bab, Aab, etc.
qualification: Applied throughout apparatus as in Exod 32:6 (πειν B* / πιειν Bab A)
